summary.title: Dev and Ops Collaboration and Awareness at Etsy and Flickr
summary.one_liner: Learn how Etsy and Flickr blended developer and operations responsibilities through shared metrics, logging, feature flags, deploy ownership and a no-blame culture.
takeaways: Everyone shares ownership of availability, performance and features rather than ops owning uptime alone.
Developers can build application-level visibility (metrics, logging, profiling) while ops provides easy platforms like Graphite and Ganglia.
Feature flags allow graceful degradation, and MTTR is prioritized over MTBF because failure response matters more than prevention.
Letting developers deploy their own code, with joint post-mortems and a no-finger-pointing culture, builds trust and shared responsibility.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck from a 2010 QCon SF talk by John Allspaw on how Etsy (and Flickr practices) combined development and operations work. It covers deploy statistics and incident metrics, the shift from ops-only ownership to shared ownership, and tooling such as Graphite, Ganglia, custom per-request logging and an in-app I/O profiler. It also describes feature flags for graceful degradation, the argument that MTTR matters more than MTBF, and cultural norms like no finger-pointing and joint post-mortems. The page text is slide content only, so detail is limited to the slide bullets.
